definition: GRIT is a quality associated with persisting in repeated practice and maintaining behavior in pursuit of a goal. In learning contexts, higher grit is linked with sticking with effort over time and building confidence through mastery experiences.

reasons: The packet supports grit as persistence through repeated practice and sustained behavior, but it does not establish this as a learning-context definition; the source is about physical activity and exercise-specific self-efficacy, not learning generally.

The phrase about 'building confidence through mastery experiences' is supported only in the narrow sense that repeated practice can accumulate mastery experiences and strengthen self-efficacy; the definition broadens this beyond what the packet states.

The definition adds a general statement that higher grit is linked with maintaining behavior in pursuit of a goal, but the packet only says self-efficacy is a proximal determinant of initiation and maintenance of behavior and that grit may channel into sustained physical activity; that causal linkage is more specific than the source supports.

The definition frames the construct specifically as applying to “learning contexts,” but the provided packet describes students in relation to physical activity (PA) and self-efficacy, not learning contexts as such.

The packet does not explicitly support the statement that higher grit is “linked with sticking with effort over time” in learning settings; it supports persistence through repeated practice and related mastery-confidence mechanisms, but within the PA/self-efficacy framing shown.
